snippet.title: Susume! Kaizoku [進め! 海賊] Game Sample - Playstation
snippet.description:
SK (sometimes called "Be Pirates!: Susume! Kaizoku" or "Be Pirates!: Go! Pirates") is an interesting game from Artdink, the same company that has made several obscure hits (Some including "No One Can Stop Mr. Domino" and the "Carnage Heart" games). Sure, Atlus and Xseed publish some niche games and such, but Artdink was also pretty popular for publishing and/or developing niche games in Japan. This particular game was only released in Japan (to my knowledge), despite how Non-Japanese it may look in style and form. At first glance, the game looks like crap for a game that was made in late 1998 (really, it might as well had came out in 1999)...and it does have crappy visuals. Thankfully, visuals aren't really the focus of the game.

The game deals with the Ankh of Might, a secret treasure that is said to exist at the end of the sea. It is rumored that the Ankh will grant any wish that the discoverer desires. However, it is also said that the treasure is protected by an immortal and that the Ankh has slowly been weakening over the centuries. The pirate king, known as Captain Flint (King of the Seven Seas AKA Thomas Flint), is aiming to find "The Eighth Sea", where the treasure is said to be. However, he is lost at sea and his boat is burned to rubble, though a few of his crew tell others of Flint's sad fate...and so you get to choose one of two people; Roger Flint (ロジャー・フリント), Captain Flint's son or Sarah Tarnitze (サラ・ターニッツ), a beautiful young woman who was chosen as a successor in Captain Flint's place and was his last bride (she used to be a dancer as well).

The game is about collecting treasure, protecting your "base", where you keep treasure, talking to townsfolk, and getting newer boats and crew members. You can sail around in 3D environments firing cannon balls at enemies to damage their ship and make stealing their ship and treasure easier. Victory slowly increases stats as well as your reputation in the world. You also can get 100 types of treasure in the game as well as equipment and such to help boost your abilities.  You will also fight on land at times and the game will be easier or harder depending on your crew setup. You have three types of allies; weak but fast types that quickly cover terrain, balanced types, and strong but slow guys. Depending on the situation, you may form a wall of strong guys, or have a few fast guys in case of an emergency...or you can use balanced units. 

Since I mentioned ships, I should also mention that they have various statistics. You can use smaller ships that are quicker, or you can use larger ships that have more durability and can hold more pirates in them (to make the battles when you board an enemy ship easier). Honestly, I feel that the bigger the boat is, the better; I see no major reason to use the small boats after chapter one...anyway, you form groups, steal stuff from other pirates, blah, blah, blah. The game may look very complex on the surface, but the game (for the most part) has a simple enough interface and is fun for a little while. It doesn't have good graphics and the soundtrack isn't anything to write home about, but it gets the job done.

Not Artdink's best effort, but it's cheap now and worth the low price it currently goes for. Enjoy. Arr!
